dict.string: OWNER APPROVED 2026-08-31; COUNSEL REVIEW PENDING. This marking does not state or imply that counsel reviewed these terms. Win's VPN Inc. operates the service. Win Empire LLC designs and builds the software and infrastructure. Win's VPN Inc. is a Florida nonprofit corporation, filing document number N26000008302, with business phone (424) 946-7876 and principal operations in Florida. The Internal Revenue Service determined, in a letter dated July 21, 2026, that Win's VPN Inc. is exempt from federal income tax under Internal Revenue Code Section 501(c)(3), with an effective date of exemption of June 11, 2026, and classified Win's VPN Inc. as a public charity under Section 509(a)(2) rather than a private foundation; the Employer Identification Number is 42-3223917. Donors can deduct contributions under IRC Section 170, and Win's VPN Inc. is qualified to receive tax-deductible bequests, devises, transfers, or gifts under Section 2055, 2106, or 2522. Contributions are deductible to the extent allowed by law, deductibility depends on each donor's own circumstances, and Win's VPN Inc. does not provide tax advice. Win's VPN Inc. uses a December 31 accounting period and is required to file an annual Form 990-series return. Tax-exempt status is a determination about the organization; it is not an IRS review, approval, or endorsement of the Win's VPN service. Win's VPN is a privacy, cybersecurity, and anti-censorship service. By activating or using Win's VPN, you agree to use the service lawfully, not attack or abuse our services or infrastructure, and accept the Terms, Verified No Log Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Hold Harmless Agreement, Limitation of Liability, and Electronic Records consent. The 1 Month and 1 Year plans are recurring PayPal subscriptions charged at the interval shown until canceled. Cancel in PayPal before the next billing date to stop future payments. Canceling partway through a period already paid for ends access when PayPal reports the cancellation, not at the end of that period, and the unused part is not refunded. Purchases are final and non-refundable to the maximum extent permitted by law, without limiting non-waivable rights. Full terms: https://www.winsvpn.org/billing/. The service must not be used for unlawful activity, abuse, torrenting, malware, intrusion, spam, copyright infringement, payment or device-limit evasion, or activity that harms third parties. Free access, trial access, donated access, and administrator-granted premium access are discretionary, non-paid, revocable access. To the maximum extent permitted by law, users of free, trial, donated, or administrator-granted access receive the service without paid-service remedies, waive claims against Win's VPN Inc. and Win Empire LLC arising from that discretionary access, and remain responsible for their own conduct, misuse, local-law compliance, and third-party claims. We may suspend access, preserve evidence, cooperate with lawful process when required, and seek recovery of damages, costs, and fees caused by misuse, abuse, attacks, or unlawful conduct. Win's VPN does not collect or keep VPN activity logs. Win's VPN does not log browsing history, DNS query history, traffic contents, raw VPN traffic, or user destination activity. Limited service metadata may be stored to operate the service, including account status, payment/referral status, legal acceptance evidence, security/abuse-prevention records, device-limit metadata, and 30-day free-access connection events. A free event records that a connection happened and which gateway served it, never what was done through it; paid accounts do not generate those events. "Verified No Log" is Win's VPN's name for these commitments and has not been independently audited or attested as of this version. So that the app can still reach a working gateway when the usual DNS or CDN paths are censored, it also requests a small gateway-recovery file hosted on GitHub at raw.githubusercontent.com; GitHub necessarily receives the connection IP and ordinary request metadata for that request, the file only selects among gateways already built into the signed app, and no account number, device identifier, or other user data is sent with it. To throttle repeated failed attempts and protect accounts, gateways, and infrastructure, the service keeps short-lived request counters and security-event records keyed to a hashed form of the source IP address, device identifier, or account number rather than to the address itself; those records exist only for security, fraud prevention, abuse response, and device-limit enforcement and never contain VPN traffic, browsing history, DNS queries, or destination activity. Only after the user asks to show the approximate-location map, before the VPN connects, the app asks first-party Win's VPN origins and gateways for an IP-derived map scene and uses Cloudflare's speed.cloudflare.com/meta as the final fallback. Those services receive the pre-VPN connection IP. Apple Maps receives the region and connection IP on Apple platforms; a first-party Win's VPN endpoint serves OpenStreetMap-derived tiles on other platforms; Win's VPN does not request device GPS for this feature or retain the returned IP, city, postal code, or map-view history. The app also generates a long-lived cryptographic key pair on first use of each account and derives a public key from it, transmitting that public key to Win's VPN with every account verification and configuration renewal request as a long-lived linkable device identifier for connection provisioning, the three-device limit, and abuse prevention; it is not derived from hardware or advertising identifiers and the account-side record is deleted or overwritten when the device is deactivated, replaced, or no longer needed. When the user runs the in-app speed test, the app measures throughput against speed.cloudflare.com and cachefly.cachefly.net for every region, and, for nodes in the western United States, losangeles.ca.speedtest.frontier.com, lsanca-speedtest-ookla-02.st.charter.com, and speedtest.lax2.sonic.net; each receives the connection IP, ordinary request metadata, and the transferred measurement traffic, with no account number, device identifier, or other app data included, and only while the test is running. Transient connection/session state is cleared when the VPN disconnects. Device-limit metadata is deleted or overwritten when the device is deactivated, replaced, or no longer needed for active account operation, and app-collected operational data that is no longer needed is deleted or anonymized within 90 days, except where longer retention is required for payment, legal, security, fraud-prevention, dispute-resolution, or active-account operation. Win Empire LLC maintains internal IP/open-source license compliance, written quality control, release testing, change management, customer acceptance, and company signoff procedures. Android and iOS launcher icon camouflage and Android/iOS in-app calculator camouflage are user-safety features for high-risk censorship environments, including Burma/Myanmar, where a visible VPN interface can expose users to retaliation. On Android and iOS both are applied automatically once a device is activated and cannot be switched off in the app; the real interface is shown after the PIN is entered. Android TV and desktop builds have neither. They do not hide malicious activity, iOS may display an operating-system confirmation when changing the icon, and the operating system's VPN status remains visible while a tunnel is active. Trusted contact and duress response: Win's VPN does not ship this feature. There is no duress code, no duress wipe, and no trusted-contact alert on any platform, including Android and iOS. No duress credential can be enrolled, no trusted-contact phone number or email is requested or stored, the Android release build declares no SMS permission and sends no SMS, and the app sends no contact, coordinate, or alert to Win's VPN servers or to any third party. Win's VPN includes third-party open-source components governed by their own licenses and notices; those upstream projects are separate from Win's VPN Inc. and Win Empire LLC and do not sponsor or endorse Win's VPN. Win's VPN Inc. and Win Empire LLC maintain insurance-readiness controls and may seek cyber or Technology Errors and Omissions coverage. No particular policy is represented as bound or in force. Coverage must be confirmed from a current binder or issued policy. If coverage exists, it creates no service warranty, direct claim right, third-party beneficiary status, guaranteed recovery, or higher liability cap for a customer or third party. The service is provided without a guarantee that every network, country, website, app, streaming service, device, or censorship system will be reachable at all times. These terms are governed by Florida law except where non-waivable consumer laws require otherwise. English is the controlling legal version; translations are convenience-only.

OWNER APPROVED 2026-08-31; COUNSEL REVIEW PENDING. This marking does not state or imply that counsel reviewed this policy. Privacy Policy. Win's VPN processes only the data needed to provide and protect the service. Before you accept this policy, the app uses only protected local settings needed to remember your choice. It does not read a device hardware identifier, request coarse public-IP location or map tiles, fetch VPN nodes or other network data, run tunnel or speed-test smoke checks, or request battery-optimization changes. If you choose Not now, those operations remain off and you can reopen this bundled policy from the app.
Data processed after acceptance. For activation and the three-device limit, the app generates a random app-install identifier on the device on first run and sends it as a Device or other ID together with the device model, platform, app version, locale, selected location, capability flags, and the account number or free-access identity. The identifier is created locally and is not derived from a device hardware identifier or an advertising identifier. On Android, Windows, and Linux it is kept in the app's private storage and reinstalling the app produces a new one; on Apple platforms it is kept in the device keychain and can survive a reinstall on the same device. The identifier may be linked to the account for service functionality, account management, fraud prevention, security, abuse prevention, and device-limit enforcement. It is not used for ads or tracking, sold, or shared for advertising. Selected split-tunneling package identifiers remain in protected local settings and are passed locally to the operating-system VPN service; the full installed-app inventory is not uploaded. The app also generates a long-lived cryptographic key pair on first use of each account and derives a public key from it; that public key is transmitted to Win's VPN with every account verification and configuration renewal request, not only at activation, and acts as one of the persistent identifiers identifying this device to the service for connection provisioning, the three-device limit, and abuse prevention. It is a long-lived linkable identifier that stays the same across app relaunches and reconnects, functions as a repeatable device marker, and is not derived from hardware or advertising identifiers. It is stored in the app's private storage or the platform keychain, and the account-side record is deleted or overwritten when the device is deactivated, replaced, or no longer needed.
Network and approximate location. After acceptance, the app may contact Win's VPN gateways to obtain nodes, account status, announcements, tunnel configuration, and security updates. So that the app can still reach a working gateway when the usual DNS or CDN paths are censored, it also requests a small gateway-recovery file hosted on GitHub at raw.githubusercontent.com. GitHub necessarily receives the connection IP and ordinary request metadata for that request. That file only selects among gateways already built into the signed app, and no account number, device identifier, or other user data is sent with the request. Only after you ask to show the approximate-location map, before a VPN connection, the app asks first-party Win's VPN origins and gateways for an IP-derived map scene and uses Cloudflare's speed.cloudflare.com/meta as the final fallback. Those services receive the pre-VPN connection IP and ordinary request metadata. Apple Maps receives the requested region and connection IP on Apple platforms; on other platforms a first-party Win's VPN endpoint serves OpenStreetMap-derived tiles. Win's VPN does not request device GPS for this feature or retain the returned public IP, city, postal code, or map-view history. When the user runs the in-app speed test, the app measures throughput against third-party test servers: speed.cloudflare.com and cachefly.cachefly.net for every region, and, for nodes in the western United States, losangeles.ca.speedtest.frontier.com, lsanca-speedtest-ookla-02.st.charter.com, and speedtest.lax2.sonic.net. Each server receives the connection IP, ordinary request metadata, and the transferred measurement traffic; no account number, device identifier, or other app data is included, and these requests occur only while the user is running the speed test.
Payments, support, and providers. Account email is processed when supplied for a paid/manual account or support. PayPal processes payment details and sends Win's VPN payment confirmation metadata; Win's VPN does not receive or store raw card data. SMTP2GO processes transactional email. Hosting, CDN, security, app-store, and platform providers process the minimum data needed for their functions. If an account is created through a referral link, the referring account is recorded against the referred account so that the account-validity bonus can be granted and reversed if the payment is refunded or cancelled. Support messages are processed only when the user supplies them. A distribution platform may provide aggregated crash or diagnostic information under its own controls; the app has no crash or analytics SDK and does not upload crash reports. Website analytics or ad-conversion events are processed only with website consent and are separate from VPN tunnel traffic. Data may be disclosed to authorities only when required by valid legal process.
Abuse prevention and rate limiting. To throttle repeated failed attempts and protect accounts, gateways, and infrastructure, the service keeps short-lived request counters and security-event records keyed to a hashed form of the source IP address, device identifier, or account number rather than to the address itself. These records exist only for security, fraud prevention, abuse response, and device-limit enforcement. They are not used to profile a user, are not used for advertising, and never contain VPN traffic, browsing history, DNS queries, or destination activity.
Trusted contact and duress response. Win's VPN does not ship this feature. There is no duress code, no duress wipe, and no trusted-contact alert on any platform, including Android and iOS. No duress credential can be enrolled, no trusted-contact phone number or email is requested or stored, the Android release build declares no SMS permission and sends no SMS, and the app sends no contact, coordinate, or alert to Win's VPN servers or to any third party.
No VPN activity logs. Win's VPN does not collect or keep browsing history, DNS query history, traffic contents, raw VPN traffic, or destination activity and does not sell personal or sensitive data. Free-access verification and sign-out create a 30-day event containing the shared free identity, device and source-IP buckets, device public-key fingerprint, platform and device model, selected gateway, stealth choice, a user-agent hash, and time. It records that a free connection happened and which gateway served it, never what was done through it; paid accounts do not generate these events. Transient connection/session state is cleared when the VPN disconnects. Device-limit metadata is deleted or overwritten when a device is deactivated, replaced, or no longer needed. App-collected operational data no longer needed is deleted or anonymized within 90 days, except while required for active-account operation, payment or accounting, legal acceptance, security, fraud prevention, abuse response, or dispute resolution. Request access, correction, deletion, or privacy help at privacy@winsvpn.org or support@winsvpn.org. Where applicable law provides additional portability, restriction, objection, appeal, or regulator-complaint rights, request them at privacy@winsvpn.org. Jurisdiction-specific legal bases, transfer mechanisms, and representative duties remain counsel-pending. "Verified No Log" is Win's VPN's name for these commitments and has not been independently audited or attested as of this version. English is the controlling version; translations are for convenience.
